source_metadata.title: Non-toxigenic penicillin-resistant cutaneous C. diphtheriae infection: A case report and review of the literature
source_metadata.source_type: short report; single-patient case report with narrative literature review
source_metadata.journal: Journal of Infection and Public Health

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors report a non-toxigenic Corynebacterium diphtheriae cutaneous infection in a previously healthy 14-year-old girl acquired in Ethiopia and presenting in the United Kingdom, emphasizing penicillin resistance.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Here, we report a case of non-toxigenic Corynebacterium diphtheriae

population.label: Previously healthy 14-year-old girl with travel-associated cutaneous infection

atoms.canonical_statement: The patient was a 14-year-old girl with no significant past medical history, born in Ethiopia, living in the United Kingdom since early childhood, and reported to be up to date with diphtheria vaccination including a 2009 booster.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A 14-year-old girl with no significant past medical history

population.label: Previously healthy 14-year-old girl with travel-associated cutaneous infection

atoms.canonical_statement: The patient returned from a one-month stay in Ethiopia one day before presentation and had cut her right lower leg on a rusty metal gate about three weeks earlier; the wound became increasingly painful, continued to discharge yellow fluid, and did not heal.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: three weeks prior to her presentation, she cut her right lower leg

population.label: Previously healthy 14-year-old girl with travel-associated cutaneous infection

concept.text: Traumatic skin wound from rusty metal gate

exposures.details: Right lower leg injury approximately three weeks before presentation

atoms.canonical_statement: At presentation she had several bilateral ulcerated lesions on the lower legs and soles with foul-smelling discharge; she was afebrile, did not look ill, and otherwise had an unremarkable examination.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: several bilateral ulcerated skin lesions on her lower legs and the soles of feet

population.label: Previously healthy 14-year-old girl with travel-associated cutaneous infection

atoms.canonical_statement: A later clinical review identified fresh-water exposure and exposure to sheep, expanding the differential diagnosis to include PVL-producing Staphylococcus aureus, cutaneous diphtheria, Aeromonas, and enterohaemorrhagic E. coli.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Fresh water exposure and exposure to sheep was uncovered in a later review

population.label: Previously healthy 14-year-old girl with travel-associated cutaneous infection

atoms.canonical_statement: Initial inpatient antimicrobial treatment consisted of intravenous benzylpenicillin plus intravenous flucloxacillin; Infectious Diseases subsequently stopped benzylpenicillin and continued flucloxacillin while additional diagnostic testing was pursued.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: initially prescribed IV benzylpenicillin and IV flucloxacillin

population.label: Previously healthy 14-year-old girl with travel-associated cutaneous infection

atoms.canonical_statement: The diagnostic work-up included a malaria film, stool and wound cultures, and a specific request to culture skin swabs on Hoyle's agar for Corynebacterium diphtheriae.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: request was made for her skin swabs to be put onto Hoyle's agar

atoms.canonical_statement: Group A Streptococcus was isolated from the skin swabs; flucloxacillin was replaced with benzylpenicillin, but the cellulitis did not improve as expected.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Group A Streptococcus was isolated from her skin swabs

population.label: Previously healthy 14-year-old girl with travel-associated cutaneous infection

exposures.details: used after Group A Streptococcus isolation

atoms.canonical_statement: Black colonies grew on Hoyle's agar and Gram staining showed Gram-positive bacilli.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Black colonies grew on the Hoyle's agar

population.label: Previously healthy 14-year-old girl with travel-associated cutaneous infection

atoms.canonical_statement: A reference laboratory used PCR and ELEK testing to confirm that the Corynebacterium diphtheriae isolate was non-toxigenic.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: confirmed that the bacteria were non-toxigenic C. diphtheriae via PCR and ELEK testing

atoms.canonical_statement: Susceptibility testing was reported as showing a penicillin-resistant Corynebacterium diphtheriae isolate that remained sensitive to erythromycin.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: we isolated a C. diphtheriae that was resistant to penicillin

population.label: Previously healthy 14-year-old girl with travel-associated cutaneous infection

atoms.canonical_statement: After the C. diphtheriae result, oral erythromycin was added while intravenous benzylpenicillin was continued; by that point the patient had received flucloxacillin followed by benzylpenicillin for a total of eight days.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: PO erythromycin was added to the treatment

population.label: Previously healthy 14-year-old girl with travel-associated cutaneous infection

exposures.details: added after identification of C. diphtheriae

atoms.canonical_statement: Oral erythromycin caused nausea and vomiting and was replaced with oral azithromycin after one day.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Erythromycin caused nausea and vomiting

population.label: Previously healthy 14-year-old girl with travel-associated cutaneous infection

atoms.canonical_statement: Three days after macrolide therapy began, benzylpenicillin was stopped and four additional days of oral azithromycin were planned to complete one total week of macrolide treatment.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: a further four days of PO azithromycin such that she would receive one total week of macrolide treatment

population.label: Previously healthy 14-year-old girl with travel-associated cutaneous infection

exposures.details: planned to complete one week total macrolide therapy

atoms.canonical_statement: After three days of macrolide therapy the ulcerations were described as notably improved, and the patient was discharged home.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Her ulcerations exhibited notably improvement

population.label: Previously healthy 14-year-old girl with travel-associated cutaneous infection

atoms.canonical_statement: Public health authorities were notified when C. diphtheriae was suspected, the family was screened before non-toxigenic status was known, infection control was informed, and the patient remained in isolation from admission until the non-toxigenic result was available.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Public health was informed at the time at which C. diphtheriae was suspected

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors state that this was the first reported clinical case of penicillin-resistant Corynebacterium diphtheriae in the United Kingdom.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: first report of a clinical case of penicillin-resistant C. diphtheriae in the UK

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors consider penicillin resistance clinically important because penicillin was the recommended first-line empiric treatment for suspected diphtheria in patients without penicillin allergy.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: penicillin is the first-line recommended choice for empiric therapy

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors recommend considering non-toxigenic cutaneous diphtheria in the differential diagnosis of fully vaccinated patients with cutaneous ulcers and a recent history of foreign travel.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: non-toxigenic cutaneous Diphtheria should be considered among the differentials

atoms.canonical_statement: In their literature review, the authors report five cases of non-toxigenic C. diphtheriae infective endocarditis in Brazil over the preceding ten years, including four females aged 7-14 years, and report a mortality rate of 40%.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The mortality rate of these patients was 40%

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors summarize a Vancouver series reporting 37 cases of non-toxigenic cutaneous diphtheria over a ten-year period ending in 2007; among 33 reviewed charts, 31 cases occurred among the urban poor, a group with high rates of intravenous drug use and hepatitis C infection.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: 37 cases of non-toxigenic cutaneous diphtheria were reported in the 10-year period ending in 2007

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors summarize 25 non-toxigenic C. diphtheriae cases observed in Poland from 2004 through 2012, of which 18 were invasive; alcoholism, homelessness, hepatic cirrhosis, and dental caries were identified as risk factors, while 17% had no concomitant disease or risk factor.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Of 25 cases of non-toxigenic C. diphtheriae observed in Poland between 2004 and 2012, 18 were invasive

atoms.canonical_statement: The review notes a reported Polish case of bacteremia and infective endocarditis caused by non-toxigenic C. diphtheriae in a 38-year-old man whose only reported comorbidity was smoking 20 cigarettes per day.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A 38-year-old male whose only comorbidity was smoking 20 cigarettes per day

atoms.canonical_statement: The review notes a reported bloodstream infection of unknown origin caused by non-toxigenic C. diphtheriae in a 23-year-old man with acute myeloid leukemia.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A 23-year-old male with AML developed bacteremia

atoms.canonical_statement: The review notes a reported prosthetic mitral valve endocarditis due to non-toxigenic C. diphtheriae in a 54-year-old woman with a prosthetic mitral valve.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A 54-year-old female with a prosthetic mitral valve
